subject.title: feat(agents): agent-owned gateway terminals with operator co-attach

question: Should agent-owned terminal input follow the existing effective exec approval policy, or become a separate explicitly enabled unrestricted host-shell capability?
rationale: The branch intentionally bypasses command approvals, but existing operators may rely on exec deny, allowlist, ask, or auto modes as their host-command boundary.

options.title: Honor effective exec policy
options.body: Expose and operate the terminal only when effective gateway-host policy permits unrestricted execution, failing closed where interactive authorization cannot preserve the configured boundary.

options.title: Add explicit terminal opt-in
options.body: Create a separate disabled-by-default policy that clearly grants unrestricted interactive host-shell access independently of exec approvals.

options.title: Accept an independent shell boundary
options.body: Keep the current default and explicitly document that exec approval settings do not constrain terminal command or input actions.

recommendation.title: Honor effective exec policy
recommendation.body: Expose and operate the terminal only when effective gateway-host policy permits unrestricted execution, failing closed where interactive authorization cannot preserve the configured boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: Owns both phases of this feature and is best positioned to choose the intended security contract.
